messages.subject: DSN / Username / Password Issue on a Mac
messages.subject_clean: DSN / Username / Password Issue on a Mac
messages.body_plain:
Hi All

I have a fun issue and I hope that you can help me with it.

I am setting up a dataset so I can perform analytics on it.
It is a ~71M row database of log information segmented into 164 cohorts,
each of which I hope to separately run analytics on to identify trends over time.

I am using the book 'Data Mining with Rattle and R' as a guide and am ready to access the data using Rattle for the first time after about a month of ETL work to get the data base to where it needs to be. Its very exciting.

The database is stored in an Amazon RDS instance, which means you can access it if you have the right URL, the right username, and the right password.

I am using Rattle on a Mac Laptop to sample the data; the eventual goal is to automate the majority of the analytics queries, but for now I am accessing the data using a desktop version of rattle() so I can generate some sample output and get a sense of the scripts and what will need to be automated to turn them into a scalable script.

The specifics of the laptop are:
R version 3.0.3 Patched (2014-03-06 r65339) -- "Warm Puppy"
Platform: x86_64-apple-darwin10.8.0 (64-bit)
Version 3.0.4 r177

To access the data, I installed the Actual Technologies ODBC drivers.
(As an aside, I would NOT have chosen to pay $34 for this technology, but the Oracle MySQL ODBC driver for Mac apparently contains a known bug which prevents it from installing. The bug is apparently fixed, but there is no release date for the new driver. This is the sort of fail you expect when open source projects get commercially taken over.)

Anyway, I then set up a DSN using the Actual Technology ODBC Manager 1.0.12 (1.0.12).
As this is a Mac (can you see this coming?) it does NOT store the password in the ODBC.ini file.
No, instead it has a checkbox where you can specify that the password should be stored and accessed from the keychain.

Of course, when you do this, and then specify the DSN in Rattle(), what do you get?

> Error in sqlTables(crs$odbc) :
>   first argument is not an open RODBC channel
> In addition: Warning messages:
> 1: In odbcDriverConnect("DSN=mywonderfulDSN", believeNRows = TRUE) :
>   [RODBC] ERROR: state 08001, code 100, message [Actual][MySQL] Unable to access keychain
> 2: In odbcDriverConnect("DSN=mywonderfulDSN", believeNRows = TRUE) :
>   ODBC connection failed

If you do not check the box, RODBC on its own constructs a username from your Mac user ID and public URL, submitting no password, which will probably not work well, ever.

I tried editing the DSN, which is in /Library/ODBC, trying to add statements like 'pwd = xxxx' and 'password = xxxx' following the syntax of other lines. This caused R to freeze, become unresponsive, and I was forced to put it out its misery.

So that is my tale of woe, at least for tonight.
I'm hoping that someone with more experience and / or wisdom can help me understand what I need to do to either release the password to RODBC from the dreaded keychain, or bypass the requirement so I can get on with getting it on, data mining wise...?

Any and all help appreciated...

Thanks!

/malcolm

We seem to have an inquiry like this often… but I never know enough about the particular data source they are asking about, or Rattle’s data source specific features, to give any sort of definitive suggestions.

Scott

As you note Scott, Rattle can load any data frame defined in the current session of R by choosing the R Dataset option on the Data tab. This allows us to use the full suite of data reading functions in R to load data from any source, and to then have it available in Rattle. Whether the data is loaded from CSV or ODBC within Rattle or from the R console, Rattle treats it exactly the same once it has been loaded as a data.frame. The Log tab in Rattle shows the actual commands that Rattle runs - and we will see there it is simply doing a read.csv().

messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the error reports.

The work around you suggest probably indicates R is finding an older version of Gtk+ - rattle_macosx.ui is a snapshot of an older version of the GUI file and uses some deprecated (i.e., very old) Gtk+ features and hence the work around for systems with old versoins of Gtk+ installed. Can you upgrade your version of Gtk+ on CentOS? Also make sure you are using the latest version of Rattle. CentOS is not a system I test on, but the recent round of testing assured that Rattle Version 3.0.4 (r177) works out of the box on Ubuntu (the Gold Standard), Windows and Mac OS/X.

Graham Williams
